title: TMiner: A Vertex-Based Task Scheduling Architecture for Graph Pattern Mining
problem: Graph pattern mining is computation- and memory-intensive with irregular memory access. After exploiting parallelism, memory access becomes the primary bottleneck due to redundant and inefficient memory access patterns in existing approaches.
motivation: Optimizing memory performance in graph pattern mining is critical for achieving high performance in a fundamentally memory-bounded workload.
method: TMiner is a combined software and hardware system designed to speed up graph pattern mining—the process of finding repeated patterns in networks of connected data points—by fixing the main bottleneck: redundant and inefficient memory access. It combines three techniques: splitting tasks so different processors handle non-overlapping sets of neighboring nodes to eliminate duplicate memory fetches; organizing shared data at compile time to keep related information close in memory; and watching which tasks have similar memory access patterns at runtime, then automatically moving and combining them to maximize data reuse. The system includes a DIMM-based near-memory architecture that exploits DRAM's internal bandwidth by placing compute and storage close together.
key_novelty: At runtime, the system identifies which tasks access memory in similar patterns and automatically moves or merges them to maximize data reuse.
contributions: Task partitioning approach based on disjoint neighbor vertex set access to reduce inter-PE redundancy
Compilation-time neighbor vertex information coalescing for improved data locality
Runtime dynamic task scheduling and merging based on memory access similarity
DIMM-based near-memory processing architecture with extended ISA
